title: 4-round AES-192: Conditional13-parameter cross-set difference

target.description: 4 inner AES rounds without initial whitening, including MixColumns in every round; fixed keys and explicitly conditioned input structures.

setting.key_relation: Fixed standard AES key schedule; component derivations treat its round-key bytes as constants, not as a related-key oracle.
setting.key_population: General key under the source's modeled internal-parameter events; no special master-key class is specified.
setting.plaintext_model: Corollary1 specifies 2^80 sets of 32 active-byte values: 2^16 combinations in other first-column entries and 2^64 choices for remaining entries. The p147 description reverses which constants these coordinates affect; this alone does not invalidate first-column collision sampling.
assumptions: Probabilities for internal parameters use the paper's randomness assumptions; they are not independently established for all AES keys.

At a fixed key and common active input, the source’s sufficient equality c1..c16 forces identical passive plaintext contexts. A useful distinct-set collision cannot be certified by that equality. Other function collisions with unequal parameter descriptions are not ruled out.

property.statement: When the first three third-round diagonal functions coincide across two sets, the fourth-round first-byte cross-set difference is \(S(C_{44}^{(3)}) \oplus S(\widetilde{C}_{44}^{(3)})\), described by13 shared/pair-specific byte parameters.
property.quantifier: The source claims distinct sets sharing c1..c16 and the same fixed key. The conditional identity survives, but independent analysis finds only identical AES contexts under that sufficient certificate; no useful distinct-set occurrence probability is established.
property.scope: Cross-set f(a11) XOR g(a11), unlike the within-set 15-parameter difference. The formal cancellation identity holds, but the proof’s equal-c1..c16 certificate forces the same fixed-key AES context and yields only a trivial zero difference.

validation.description: Formal equal-parameter substitutions verify the cancellation identity. Two independent GF(256) derivations find rank 12 for c5..c16 as an affine map of the 12 non-first-column S(round1) bytes, and rank 3 for c1..c4 on the other diagonal inputs. Thus equal c1..c16 implies identical first-round states and identical passive plaintexts. The derivation is exact; finite source-graph checks are not an end-to-end attack reproduction.

field_conflicts.label: Reversed parameter-dependency description
field_conflicts.description: With standard ShiftRows, changing passive first-column input bytes leaves c1..c4 fixed and can change c5..c8, reversing the p147 dependency explanation. An actual AES equal-c1..c8 pair has identical C3_11 functions for all 256 active values. This local discrepancy does not require replacing first-column sampling with diagonal coordinates.

observations.locator: Printed pp.145–146 ShiftRows definition and first-round state expression
observations.reported: The first MixColumns column depends on diagonal input bytes a11,a22,a33,a44. First-column passive changes instead affect later offsets; a finite actual-AES C3_11 collision witness confirms first-column sampling is possible.

field_conflicts.label: Equal-parameter proof admits only identical AES contexts
field_conflicts.description: For fixed round keys and a common active input, c5..c16 is a rank-12 affine map of the 12 external S(round1) bytes. Together with c1..c4 equality, this fixes the whole first-round state; AES invertibility forces the same passive plaintext context. All four third-round functions then coincide, so the cross-set difference is zero. This challenges only the source’s literal distinct-set equal-parameter certificate and its 2^-64 generation model, not the formal conditional identity or every possible function collision.

observations.reported: The proof assumes c1..c8 equal, then models c9..c16 equal with probability 2^-64 to obtain a nontrivial 13-parameter cross-set description.

observations.locator: PDF3–5/printed146–148 first-round state, corrected Equations3–6; independent reviewer derivation accepted 2026-10-26.
observations.reported: Reviewer-derived map consists of four nonsingular 3-by-3 MixColumns submatrices, total rank12. The literal certificate forces identical fixed-key, aligned-input AES contexts; unequal-parameter function collisions remain outside this conclusion.
